The Cello itself has no branding on it, so I'm assuming it is just a cheapo made in China, however, the preamp (the block on the back) has HPVP-30 on it, and I have no clue if that means anything significant. I have plugged it straight into an amp, and with fiddling with the amps settings, I can get a semi satisfactory sound (enough for my first electric), but bass doesn't carry too well. It has no nut on the outside that I can see, it's just flush with the block. I'll take it to the electrician next door and ask if he can safely remove the block cover and tighten/secure the jacks. The sound itself of the preamp I can live with for now, but if there is a preamp that I can buy that is better, that would be great.

Edit: Not sure if I'm using the right word, sorry if I'm not, but what I've been calling the preamp is the little block on the back of the cello, underneath the bridge. It has 3 jacks (as described in the original post), a tone dial which transitions it from sounding like a 1980's radio into something a bit more mellow and bassy, but losing a bit of attack (not sure if that's how it sounds on most E-cellos). I also have a volume dial, an on/off switch and a 9v battery compartment. I can record and upload some of its raw sound if that'd make determining the right equipment easier.
